trials.hypothesis: Change: flip the stem features left-right (after the learned 1x1 stem), so the per-anchor scores in the footprint head are computed over the cells the brick will actually land on. A correct placement then shows up locally, which removes the reason to collapse to DONE. Recipe stays at the default so the mirror effect is tested alone. Refuted if dev success stays near 0 and the agent still ends with DONE before any placement.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        # mirror columns so anchor x's footprint window covers the landing cells
        s = torch.flip(s, dims=[3])
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
HEADS = 4

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3, "lr": 0.001}


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=2, dilation=2)
        self.gb = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, spec.Y * spec.X, WIDTH))
        nn.init.normal_(self.pos, std=0.02)
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(WIDTH, HEADS, batch_first=True)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        s = torch.flip(s, dims=[3])
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        g0 = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(f + self.c3(f) + self.gb(g0)[:, :, None, None])
        B, C, H, W = f.shape
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        q = self.ln(t + self.pos)
        a, _ = self.attn(q, q, q, need_weights=False)
        f = f + a.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, H, W)
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

SC = 48
SF = 32
PROJ = 24
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3, "lr": 0.001}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        cin = spec.in_channels + 8 + self.Z
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, SC, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(SC, SF, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.gb = nn.Linear(2 * SF, SF)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(SF, PROJ, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        for o in self.outs:
            nn.init.zeros_(o.weight)
            nn.init.zeros_(o.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * SF, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        build = obs[:, 0:Z]
        tgt = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        miss = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        extra = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        lay = torch.stack([build, tgt, miss, extra], dim=2)
        below = F.pad(lay, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        full = obs.unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, C, Y, X)
        zid = torch.eye(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)[None, :, :, None, None].expand(B, Z, Z, Y, X)
        s = torch.cat([full, lay, below, zid], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, C + 8 + Z, Y, X)
        h = self.stem(s)
        h = torch.flip(h, dims=[3])
        hz = h.view(B, Z, SF, Y, X)
        g0 = torch.cat([hz.mean((1, 3, 4)), hz.amax((1, 3, 4))], dim=1)
        hz = F.relu(hz + self.gb(g0)[:, None, :, None, None])
        h = hz.reshape(B * Z, SF, Y, X)
        p = self.proj(h)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            u = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            u = u.view(B, Z, HID, Y, X).amax(1)
            res.append(out(u))
        place = torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([hz.mean((1, 3, 4)), hz.amax((1, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 3, "lr": 0.001}


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=2, dilation=2)
        self.gb = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        s = torch.flip(s, dims=[3])
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        g0 = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(f + self.c3(f) + self.gb(g0)[:, :, None, None])
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

        super().__init__()

        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):

        self.gb = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())

        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 2, "lr": 0.001}


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=2, dilation=2)
        self.gb = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        s = torch.flip(s, dims=[3])
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        g0 = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(f + self.c3(f) + self.gb(g0)[:, :, None, None])
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

- dev behaviour: placements per episode 10.67; episodes ending with DONE before any placement 0.0%; mean IoU 0.985; cells placed inside / outside the target per episode 24.30 / 0.47

analyses.1: The starting network collapsed to DONE on its first step (100% of dev episodes). Collapsing like this is the expected result of its layout. Each placement lands at the mirror column X-dx-x, but the placement logit for anchor x is computed from local conv features at column x, with a receptive field of only about 5 columns. So the network cannot see where its brick will land, nearly every placement earns negative reward, and DONE (reward 0) wins. The main fix is to flip the feature map left-right after the first learned 1x1 layer. After the flip, the head's window for anchor x covers exactly the cells the brick will land on, and the footprint pooling lines up. The flip only reorders positions and comes after a learned layer, so the rules allow it. The budget is a second concern: the default recipe gives only 32 PPO updates. With a 0.000 baseline and seed noise, test the flip alone, then the flip plus more updates, then the flip plus more context.
analyses.2: Mirroring the stem features left to right fixes the hidden rule. After the flip, each anchor's footprint window covers the cells where the brick actually lands, and the agent stops collapsing to DONE (0 → 0.64). Adding global context and a dilated conv (r1c3) raised the score to 0.886, and both seeds landed close together (0.86 and 0.91). The two runs without global context each had one bad seed (0.43 and 0.36). More PPO updates without context (r1c2) did not clearly help, and the gap is within seed noise. Training success in r1c3 levels off near 0.8 as the learning rate decays. The remaining failures are probably about layer and order: whether a brick lands at the correct layer given the heights under its footprint, plus the discounted +1 bonus for an exact build. This round: (1) a longer credit horizon (gamma), (2) global attention on top of r1c3, (3) a new design that processes each layer separately so the footprint pooling can check the landing layer.
analyses.3: The mirror flip is what made learning possible. Without it, the agent learned to press DONE at once (0.000). With it, scores were 0.64 to 0.89. The best trial so far is r1c3 (flip, a third residual conv with dilation 2, global context broadcast to every cell, 128-env recipe). It scored 0.886, and its two seeds agreed closely. Three changes since then did worse: gamma 0.99 (0.846, about the same within noise), cell self-attention (0.783, with fewer training steps because it costs more) and the per-layer slice encoder (0.42, clearly worse). Training success was still rising at the end of every good run (r1c3: 0.76 to 0.80 between 75% and 100%), so the budget is limiting. In r1c1 against r1c2, more and fresher updates with the same number of gradient steps raised seed-0 training success. Dev IoU is about 0.98 and few cells land outside the target, so the remaining errors are small mistakes in precision or order. This round tests three cheap ways to learn more within the budget: more updates, more samples from a cheaper network, and a sharper policy from a lower entropy bonus.
analyses.4: Flipping the features left-right is the change that matters: without it the agent always learns to stop at DONE, and with it dev success goes from 0 to 0.64–0.89. The best result is r1c3 (flip plus global context, 0.886), and both its seeds score well. None of the later changes beat it. Gamma 0.99 scored 0.846, which is within noise. Self-attention scored 0.78 and cut the sample budget. The per-layer encoder scored 0.42. The slim network with more samples scored 0.870, which ties r1c3, so width barely matters. Two results point at entropy and seed stability. Lowering ent_coef to 0.003 made both seeds worse (0.74), which suggests more exploration might help. Halving n_envs led to a full collapse to DONE on one seed. Dev IoU is about 0.98 and roughly 0.3–0.5 cells per episode land outside the target, so the remaining errors are a few wrong placements per design. For this last round I make three single changes to r1c3: a higher entropy bonus, fewer PPO epochs to get more samples, and a uniform starting policy.
